title: Shelf by Shelf - Part One
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zyY2aRVZMp4

Daniel (@dungeondive) launches Shelf by Shelf, a series born from viewer requests for more book content: a slow amble along his bookshelves, one or two shelves per episode, in no particular order because he's never alphabetised anything in his life. Part One is dominated by two towering figures. First, Philip K. Dick — the full run of vintage 1990s paperbacks that hooked him in high school, with a collector's love for mismatched covers and doubles. He offers a starter's list: *Martian Time-Slip*, *Ubik*, *The Three Stigmata of Palmer Eldritch*, *A Scanner Darkly*, *Dr. Bloodmoney* and *Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said* — while cheerfully dismissing *A Maze of Death* as PKD's worst. He moves to Lord Dunsany, "the ultimate writer of fantasy" and direct ancestor of both Tolkien and Lovecraft, including a volume that once sat on Tolkien's own shelf. Finally he champions J.M. McDermott, whom he calls the most underrated author working today; *Last Dragon* is his all-time favourite fantasy novel, "Miyazaki meets Gene Wolfe." A warm, opinionated tour that doubles as a reading list.

----

Where would you start a newcomer on Philip K. Dick — does Daniel's six-book list match your own, or is there an obvious omission?
